source_binding.paper: Training Agents to Self-Report Misbehavior, arXiv:2602.22303

official_artifact_support.main_repository: The paper's main code repository is public and explicitly maps evaluation-iterative-adversarial/ to Sec. 5.1 / App. H.
official_artifact_support.full_pipeline_dependencies: The README states the paper pipeline spans brucewlee/self-incrimination, brucewlee/synthetic-scheming and brucewlee/mini-control-arena; fine-tuning is performed through OpenAI/Vertex APIs.
official_artifact_support.adaptive_optimization_code: evaluation-iterative-adversarial contains configs.py, optimizer.py, runner.py, run_eval.py, OOD transfer and post-hoc monitoring scripts.
official_artifact_support.documented_protocol: The directory README documents a seed prompt followed by 10 iterations; each iteration has a proposer generate 6 variants, a pruner select 3, and evaluation on optimization/held-out splits, with OOD transfer to four SHADE Arena tasks.
official_artifact_support.defense_binding: configs.py pins dated GPT-4.1 base/monitor model names and exact OpenAI fine-tuned model identifiers for the self-incrimination and honesty defenses. Strong and weak monitoring configs and combined report_scheming+monitoring configs are explicit.
official_artifact_support.environment_lock: requirements.txt pins a large Python dependency set including inspect-ai==0.3.144, openai==2.7.1 and anthropic==0.72.0, but external model-service behavior and the editable mini-control-arena checkout are not frozen by this file alone.
official_artifact_support.training_data: The main README shares paper fine-tuning-data links and exact OpenAI fine-tuning hyperparameters (including seed 1234) for several methods.
official_artifact_support.raw_result_availability: The repository's .gitignore excludes logs/, results/, runs/, outputs/, checkpoints/, JSONL and evaluation-*/logs*/. The adaptive-evaluation README says history.json and per-iteration .eval outputs are written under logs/, but those paper-run result logs are not tracked in the audited commit.

reported_failure_evidence.paper_primary_claims: The paper/project materials report that adversarial optimization degrades several defenses; for Code Backdooring, Just Ask increases from 28% to 68% undetected successful attack rate. The paper also reports degradation of strong monitoring on Code Backdooring while a combined self-incrimination+strong-monitoring defense is hardest to break in the tested conditions.
reported_failure_evidence.worker_scope: FE-074 correctly uses this as evidence that static/fixed-attack evaluation can overstate a defense when attack framing is optimized against the defense. It also correctly preserves the positive control that monitoring is not uniformly useless and combined defenses can be stronger.
reported_failure_evidence.numerical_reproduction_status: The headline adaptive-optimization numbers were not independently regenerated in this audit because the paper-run logs/trajectories are not committed and exact rerun requires external dated/proprietary model services and the companion evaluation environment.

reproducibility_assessment.judgment: FE-074 has strong author-side reproducibility support: the adaptive proposer-pruner protocol, defense/model bindings, evaluation scripts, companion environment pointers, dependency pins and fine-tuning recipes are public. However, the exact paper-run adaptive histories and trajectory/evaluation logs are intentionally untracked, so the 28%->68% and related headline cells remain primary-study numerical evidence rather than independently replayed results. The narrow failure implication—defense-aware attack optimization can materially worsen measured undetected success in these tested agent-control settings—is well supported by the paper, but no quantitative transfer to other domains is justified.

exact_blockers: Paper-run adaptive history.json/.eval/log outputs are not tracked in the audited repository commit and are excluded by .gitignore patterns.
Exact rerun depends on dated but externally served GPT-4.1/GPT-5/Gemini-family models and provider-side fine-tuned model identifiers; repository pinning cannot freeze service behavior indefinitely.
The main setup clones mini-control-arena without an exact commit pin in the top-level instructions, so a historical rerun must separately recover the companion repository revision used for the paper.
Fine-tuning requires OpenAI/Vertex API infrastructure; training data and hyperparameters are shared, but provider execution remains external.
No independent public rerun reproducing the Sec. 5.1 adaptive-optimization headline cells was found in the targeted search.
scope_guards: Do not generalize the reported attack-rate changes from APPS/BashArena/SHADE-family settings to arbitrary LLM security or all monitoring systems.
Do not infer that monitoring is useless: the paper reports condition-dependent performance and a complementary combined defense.
Do not treat the public protocol implementation as independent replication of the paper's numbers.

Do not conflate attack-prompt optimization with stronger underlying side-task capability; the paper's interpretation is that evasion is a major driver in the tested setup, not a universal decomposition theorem.
exact_next_action: Search for an archived/shared paper-run history.json or trajectory/result bundle for Sec. 5.1 and pin the exact mini-control-arena companion commit. If neither is available, retain the adaptive-evaluation numbers as strong primary-study evidence and prioritize a genuinely independent same-task rerun rather than reconstructing headline cells from figures.
